historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Proton pump inhibitors

starting.description: A reported working antisecretory compound, CMN131, supplied the starting lead for the omeprazole/PPI series. Its observed activity led to heterocyclic redesign, metabolite investigation and functional gastric experiments. The later pump model and accumulation/stability optimization did not originate the whole programme from scratch.

inspiration.description: Observed gastric antisecretory activity in a synthetic lead, followed by specific gastric proton-transport/ATPase physiology and compartmental accumulation reasoning. No natural-scaffold requirement is imposed.

steps.description: The acid-inhibition programme used Servier's reported antisecretory CMN 131 as a chemical starting clue. Its acute toxicity motivated replacement of the thioamide arrangement with heterocyclic systems, yielding active H 124/26 in 1973.

H 124/26's more potent sulphoxide metabolite timoprazole became the lead when the parent was found already patented. Substitution informed by mercaptobenzimidazole chemistry separated thyroid/thymus effects from acid inhibition and yielded picoprazole. This preserves the upstream CMN 131 chemical ancestry through those synthetic changes.

The early series showed a surprisingly prolonged acid-inhibitory action. Specific gastric-gland, vesicle and ATPase experiments then identified pump inhibition as its mechanism, supplying a physiological explanation and a more specific development direction. Fellenius et al. directly showed picoprazole inhibiting proton transport and ATPase activity.

Knowledge that weak bases accumulate in the acidic parietal-cell compartment informed pyridine substituents that raised basicity and accumulation. Together with benzimidazole substitution improving stability at neutral pH, this produced omeprazole H 168/68.

Omeprazole entered European use as Losec in 1988. The subsequent PPI succession included the cohort's lansoprazole, pantoprazole and esomeprazole, the S-enantiomer of omeprazole. This closes the founding class history without separate later-analogue biographies.

design.description: Heterocyclic redesign and metabolite selection improved the initial series; substitutions addressed thyroid/thymus effects, acidic-compartment accumulation and neutral-pH stability, leading to omeprazole. These are deliberate developments of an existing observed effect.

circumstances.description: The acid-inhibition programme and optimization were planned; the participant history calls the unusually prolonged action surprising. This does not make the entire programme accidental.

evidence.locator: p.133, Background and The omeprazole project, complete paragraphs: the late-1960s acid-inhibition programme was restarted in dogs in 1972; literature supplied Servier's active but acutely toxic CMN 131; heterocyclic redesign of its thioamide produced the active H 124/26 in 1973.

p.133, Patent problem and Toxicological challenges, complete paragraphs: H 124/26 was already patented; its more potent sulphoxide metabolite H 83/69 became timoprazole; substituent changes separated acid inhibition from thyroid/thymus effects, yielding picoprazole H 149/94.

pp.133–134, Compound optimization, complete section: isolated mucosa/glands enabled screening; pump-localization work suggested the target; adding pyridine substituents raised basicity to concentrate compound near the pump, yielding omeprazole H 168/68. The benzimidazole methoxy group improved neutral-pH stability.

p.132, introductory paragraph beginning From the late 1960s onwards: the early pump-inhibiting compounds were potent acid inhibitors with an unexpectedly prolonged action; p.133, Toxicological challenges, reports picoprazole's prolonged antisecretory action in human volunteers. The surprise coded here concerns duration, not the initial lead discovery.
p.134, Resumption of clinical studies, opening paragraph: European clinical introduction after development and trials.

p.160, main text following Fig.2 and preceding Fig.4, with Figs.2–3: picoprazole H 149/94 inhibited proton transport in gastric vesicles and the corresponding ATPase activity; human gastric preparations extended the mechanistic finding. Line-wrap hyphenation normalized.

Chemistry and Biology of PPIs, first two paragraphs: timoprazole was a synthesized pyridylmethylsulfinyl benzimidazole; omeprazole followed, then lansoprazole, pantoprazole, rabeprazole and the S-enantiomer of omeprazole. The cohort members belong to this stated class succession.

Chemistry and Biology of PPIs, first paragraph: the timoprazole synthetic antecedent and experiments showing acid-transport-dependent activation are described; the quoted date differs from S1 Figure 1's 1974 date.

limits: The classification describes the documented founding PPI/omeprazole lineage from an already active CMN131 lead. The earlier origin/design of CMN131 is not established without its1971 original report.
A synthetic starting compound and later rational pump-directed optimization do not imply whole-class design from scratch under the approved criterion.
The later class succession is established without individual analogue biographies.
conflicts: Timoprazole's synthesis is dated 1974 in S1 Figure 1 but 1975 in S3 Chemistry and Biology of PPIs. The chain is preserved without resolving the year from these sources.

The 1971 CMN 131 antecedent's publisher/search metadata include Pascaud as first author, while the retrieved PubMed display and S1 reference 3 list Malen and Danree. The DOI/title/journal/pages match; full-text author-list adjudication remains open.
gaps: The 1971 CMN 131 original report was located but not read: the publisher request returned HTTP 403 and the PubMed page supplied no abstract in this retrieval. Its chemical ancestry is therefore not independently established here.
The 1981 pump paper is original verification of the mechanism only; the earlier synthesis/metabolism and optimization history relies on the full-text discoverer retrospective.
